title: Electrical Safety SOP
text: Keep people away from water near electrical equipment. Do not touch switches or exposed wiring. Isolate the electricity supply only if a trained person can do so safely. Escalate immediately to an authorized electrician and contact emergency services when fire or electrocution risk is present.

title: Plumbing Leakage Handling Guide
text: Identify the leak location, isolate the nearest water valve when safe, protect electrical equipment, record affected units, and assign a plumber. Shared leaks across several apartments should be treated as a possible block incident.

title: Lift Emergency Procedure
text: When a person is trapped, contact lift emergency support and security, maintain communication, and never force lift doors. Restrict use until an authorized lift technician confirms safety.

title: Visitor and Security Rules
text: Visitors require a resident-linked request and security approval. Security must verify identity, record entry status, and record exit. Access is limited to the authorized block and purpose.

title: Resident Community Guidelines & Noise Policy
text: Quiet hours are strictly observed between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM. Household waste must be segregated into dry and wet bins and placed in floor chutes before 9:00 AM. Pets must be leashed in all common areas, elevators, and corridors. Balcony plants must be secured against falling hazards.

title: Amenity Booking & Clubhouse Rules
text: Residents can book the community hall, badminton court, and party terrace up to 30 days in advance via the resident portal. Clubhouse facilities are open daily from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM. A sanitization deposit applies to party hall bookings, refundable upon inspection. Cancellations 24 hours prior receive full refund.

title: Maintenance Billing & Payment FAQ
text: Monthly society maintenance bills are generated on the 1st of every month and are due by the 10th. Payments can be completed online via UPI, net banking, or cards through the SafeHome billing portal. Late fee of ₹50 per week applies for payments past the 20th. Specific repair charges are billed separately upon work order sign-off.

title: Split Air Conditioner Servicing Standard
text: Split air conditioners in apartments are serviced every 90 days during summer and every 180 days in winter. A standard service includes washing the indoor filter mesh, cleaning the evaporator coil with a foaming cleaner, flushing the condensate drain line, and checking the outdoor condenser fins for bent or blocked sections. The technician records the supply-air temperature after 15 minutes of operation; a reading above 16 degrees Celsius in cooling mode at 24 degrees setpoint indicates low refrigerant or a weak compressor. Refrigerant top-up (R32 or R410A) may only be done by a certified HVAC technician after a leak test with nitrogen pressure or an electronic detector. Topping up without fixing the leak is not permitted.

title: Troubleshooting Warm Air from AC Units
text: If an air conditioner runs but the room stays warm, first confirm the remote is in Cool mode and not Fan or Dry. Check that the indoor filter is not choked with dust, because a clogged filter is the most common cause of poor cooling in this society. Look at the outdoor unit: if its fan is not spinning or the unit is in direct afternoon sun without shade, report it. Ice formation on the copper pipes points to low gas or restricted airflow. Residents should switch the unit off if ice is seen and raise an HVAC request; do not pour water on the outdoor unit.

title: Electric Water Heater (Geyser) Safety
text: Storage water heaters must have a working pressure relief valve and a thermostat cut-off. If the geyser makes a hissing or banging noise, or water from the hot tap is steaming, switch it off at the wall switch and the MCB and raise an urgent request. Never block the relief valve outlet. A tripping RCCB when the geyser is switched on usually means a failed heating element leaking current to the tank; the unit must stay off until an electrician tests insulation resistance. Element replacement is a 45-minute job; tank corrosion requires full replacement.

title: Washing Machine and Dishwasher Water Issues
text: Water pooling under a washing machine is usually caused by a loose inlet hose, a cracked drain hose, or a blocked floor trap. Turn off the angle valve behind the machine before inspecting. Front-load machines that stop mid-cycle with water inside typically have a choked drain pump filter, which residents may clean using the access flap at the bottom front. Dishwashers that leave dirty water should have the bottom filter and spray arms cleaned. The society maintenance team services only the plumbing connections; internal appliance repairs are handled by the brand service centre at the resident cost.

title: Refrigerator Not Cooling Checklist
text: Before raising a request for a refrigerator that is not cooling, check that the plug is fully seated, the voltage stabiliser display is on, and the door gasket seals evenly. Frost build-up on the back panel of a frost-free fridge indicates a defrost heater or sensor failure. A clicking sound every few minutes with no cooling usually means the compressor relay is failing. Refrigerator repairs are not covered by society maintenance; the facility desk can share a list of empanelled appliance vendors.

title: Drain Blockage and Sewer Backflow Procedure
text: Slow drains in bathrooms are cleared with a plunger or a flexible drain snake; chemical drain cleaners are not allowed because they damage PVC stack joints. If several apartments in the same vertical line report gurgling or backflow at the same time, the shared soil stack is blocked and the facility manager must treat it as a block-level incident. The plumbing contractor then rods the stack from the ground-floor inspection chamber. Residents in the affected stack should avoid using washing machines until clearance is confirmed.

title: Wall Seepage and Dampness Diagnosis
text: Damp patches, peeling paint, or white salt deposits on a wall are signs of seepage. Seepage on a ceiling usually comes from the bathroom or balcony of the apartment directly above, so the apartment above must be inspected first. Seepage on an external wall that worsens during rain points to cracks in exterior plaster or failed window sealant. The technician uses a moisture meter and photographs the patch; ponding tests on the floor above confirm a failed waterproofing membrane. Repairs above the ceiling require consent from the upstairs resident.

title: Terrace and Overhead Tank Waterproofing
text: Terrace waterproofing is inspected every year before the monsoon in May. Top-floor apartments are most exposed to roof leaks. Overhead water tanks are cleaned every six months; the cleaning schedule is announced 48 hours in advance because water supply is cut for four hours. Any crack in the terrace membrane must be sealed with polyurethane coating, and terrace drains must be kept free of leaves to prevent ponding.

title: MCB Tripping and Power Failure in an Apartment
text: If power goes off in only one apartment, check the apartment distribution board. A tripped MCB that trips again immediately after reset indicates a short circuit on that circuit; leave it off and report it. If the RCCB trips, unplug all appliances, reset, and plug them back one by one to find the faulty appliance. If the whole floor is dark, the problem is at the floor meter room and must be handled by the society electrician. Residents must never replace fuses with copper wire or bypass an RCCB.

title: Earthing and Shock Complaints
text: A mild shock from a metal tap, washing machine body, or geyser indicates an earthing fault or current leakage. The affected appliance must be switched off immediately and not touched with wet hands. The electrician measures earth resistance at the apartment earth pit connection; values above 5 ohms require earth pit recharging. Shock complaints are always classified as high severity with a four-hour response target.

title: Piped Gas Leak Emergency
text: If a smell of gas is noticed, do not operate any electrical switch, do not light a flame, and do not use a mobile phone inside the apartment. Open windows, close the gas meter valve outside the kitchen, leave the apartment, and call the city gas distributor emergency line and security. Only the gas distributor may reopen the supply after a pressure test. The society maintenance team must not attempt gas pipeline repairs.

title: Diesel Generator Backup Operation
text: The diesel generator provides backup for lifts, common lighting, water pumps, and a limited 1 kW load per apartment. It starts automatically within 30 seconds of a grid failure. The facility manager logs fuel level daily and the generator is run on load for 15 minutes every Monday. Annual load bank testing and a pollution-control check are mandatory under the AMC.

title: Fire Alarm and Sprinkler Testing
text: Smoke detectors and manual call points are tested every quarter by the fire safety vendor, one floor at a time, with an announcement to residents. Sprinkler heads must not be painted or covered. If a fire alarm sounds, residents should use staircases and never lifts, and gather at the assembly point near the main gate. False alarms caused by cooking smoke should still be reported so the detector can be inspected.

title: Pest Control Schedule
text: General pest control for common areas is done on the first Saturday of every month. Apartment-level cockroach gel treatment is available on request and is billed per apartment. Termite treatment is done for wooden doors and wardrobes when tunnels or powdery residue are noticed; the treatment requires the apartment to be vacated for six hours.

title: Recurring Issue Escalation Policy
text: An issue is classed as recurring when the same category of fault is reported for the same apartment three or more times within 90 days, or when the same asset fails twice within 30 days of a repair. Recurring issues are escalated to the facility manager, who must review the previous repair notes, assign a senior technician instead of the original one, and consider root-cause work such as pipe replacement rather than another patch repair. The resident is informed of the escalation.

title: Technician Assignment and SLA Policy
text: Requests are assigned to a technician whose skill matches the category and who covers the block. Critical requests such as electrical shock, gas smell, lift entrapment, or active flooding have a one-hour response target. High severity requests have four hours, medium requests one working day, and low requests three working days. If the assigned technician is unavailable, the facility manager reassigns within 30 minutes. Technicians must close a ticket with resolution notes and photos.

title: Lift Annual Maintenance Contract
text: Each block has two passenger lifts covered by a comprehensive annual maintenance contract with monthly preventive visits. The lift vendor must respond to entrapment calls within 30 minutes. Lift ropes are inspected every quarter and the statutory lift licence is renewed annually after inspection by the electrical inspectorate.

title: RO Water Purifier and Water Quality
text: Drinking water in the society comes from municipal supply and borewell water treated at the central water treatment plant. Apartment RO purifiers need filter replacement every six months and membrane replacement every two years. If tap water turns yellow or smells, residents should stop drinking it and report it; the facility manager checks the treatment plant and overhead tank chlorination.

title: Door, Window and Carpentry Repairs
text: Main doors that do not close properly usually need hinge screw tightening or door-closer adjustment. Sliding balcony doors that are hard to move need track cleaning and roller replacement. Carpentry repairs inside apartments are chargeable, while repairs to common-area doors and fire doors are covered by the society.

title: Preventive Maintenance Calendar
text: The preventive maintenance calendar covers water pump servicing every month, overhead tank cleaning every six months, DG servicing every 250 running hours, fire system testing every quarter, terrace waterproofing inspection every May, and AC servicing for common areas every 90 days. Overdue items are flagged on the facility dashboard.

title: Water Pump and Low Pressure Complaints
text: Low water pressure on upper floors usually indicates a pressure pump fault or a partially closed riser valve. If only one apartment has low pressure, the inlet filter or the apartment isolation valve is checked. Water pumps are serviced monthly; a pump making grinding noise must be stopped and the standby pump started.

title: Moving Heavy Furniture and Service Lift Use
text: Heavy furniture and appliances must be moved using the service lift with protective padding, only between 9:00 AM and 6:00 PM. A refundable damage deposit is collected for move-in and move-out. Any damage to lift panels or corridor walls is deducted from the deposit after inspection.
